name: Guest Permissions Orchestrator${{APP_NAME_SUFFIX}}
description: Runs and investigates guest-permission discovery across Entra and Azure by orchestrating pipeline runs, telemetry queries, and dashboard pivots.

conversation_starters.title: 🟢 L100: Open Dashboard
conversation_starters.text: Get the Grafana endpoint and give me the direct dashboard link for the Guest Permissions Command Center.

conversation_starters.title: 🟢 L100: Latest Run Status
conversation_starters.text: What was the status of the most recent guest-permissions pipeline run?

conversation_starters.title: 🟢 L100: What Can You Do
conversation_starters.text: In plain language, what can you help me investigate about guest access?

conversation_starters.title: 🔵 L200: Run Pipeline Now
conversation_starters.text: Start a fresh guest-permissions pipeline run for rg-entra-permissions and confirm the execution ID.

conversation_starters.title: 🔵 L200: Check Run Health
conversation_starters.text: Show the last 5 pipeline executions and flag any that failed or ran too long.

conversation_starters.title: 🔵 L200: Explain One Guest
conversation_starters.text: Query telemetry for one guest user and summarize their Entra permissions plus Azure resource permissions.

conversation_starters.title: 🟠 L300: Compare Two Guests
conversation_starters.text: Compare two guests' effective access and tell me specifically which one holds their role directly and which one inherits it through a group.

conversation_starters.title: 🟠 L300: Run Then Verify
conversation_starters.text: Run the pipeline, then cross-reference the new execution's run ID against telemetry to confirm the data actually refreshed.

conversation_starters.title: 🟠 L300: PIM vs Active
conversation_starters.text: For a given guest, tell me whether their highest-privilege role is currently active or only PIM-eligible, and what activating it would require.

conversation_starters.title: 🔴 L400: Risk Ranking
conversation_starters.text: Across all current guests, which one has the broadest effective access and which has the narrowest? Justify the ranking using scope breadth, role power, and whether access is direct, inherited, or eligible.

conversation_starters.title: 🔴 L400: Deny Logic Limits
conversation_starters.text: If a guest has a role assignment and a matching deny assignment at the same scope, what can you actually detect from telemetry versus what requires a separate Azure RBAC check-access call? Be explicit about the limitation.

conversation_starters.title: 🔴 L400: KQL Deep Dive
conversation_starters.text: Query pipeline telemetry for every distinct effective scope type one guest has a role on, with a count of resources per scope type, and flag anything that looks anomalous.

disclaimer.text: This agent orchestrates control-plane scans and telemetry. Verify destructive remediation changes through your IAM approval workflow.
